The '''American Cryptogram Association''' ('''ACA''') is an American [[non-profit]] organization devoted to the [[hobby]] of [[cryptography]], with an emphasis on types of codes, ciphers, and [[cryptograms]] that can be solved either with pencil and paper, or with computers, but not computer-only systems.

==History==

The ACA was formed on September 1, 1930. Initially the primary interest was in monoalphabetic [[substitution ciphers]] (also known as "single alphabet" or "Aristocrat" puzzles). This has since been extended to dozens of different systems, such as [[Playfair cipher|Playfair]], [[autokey cipher|autokey]], [[Transposition (cryptography)|transposition]], and [[Vigenère ciphers]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=History {{!}} American Cryptogram Association |url=https://www.cryptogram.org/about-the-aca/history/ |access-date=2026-03-07 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Since some of its members had belonged to the “[[National Puzzlers' League]]”, some of the NPL terminology ("nom," "Krewe," etc.) is also used in the ACA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History {{!}} American Cryptogram Association |url=https://www.cryptogram.org/about-the-aca/history/ |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260107045618/https://www.cryptogram.org/about-the-aca/history/ |archive-date=2026-01-07 |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=www.cryptogram.org |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Publications and activities==
The association has a collection of books and articles on cryptography and related subjects in the library at [[Kent State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cryptography Manuscripts collection {{!}} Special Collections and Archives {{!}} Kent State University Libraries |url=https://www.library.kent.edu/special-collections-and-archives/cryptography-manuscripts-collection |access-date=2026-06-26 |website=www.library.kent.edu |language=en}}</ref>

An annual convention takes place in late August or early September. Recent conventions have been held in [[Bletchley Park]] and [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Constitution {{!}} American Cryptogram Association |url=https://www.cryptogram.org/about-the-aca/constitution/ |access-date=2026-03-07 |language=en-US}}</ref>

There is also a regular journal called “''The Cryptogram''”, which first appeared in February, 1932, and has grown to a 28-page bimonthly periodical which includes articles and challenge ciphers.<ref name=":0" />

==Notable members==
{{unreferenced section|date=June 2023}}
* [[Herbert Yardley|H. O. Yardley]], who used the nom BOZO, first Vice President in 1933.
* [[Helen Fouché Gaines]], member since 1933, who used the nom PICCOLA, editor of the 1939 book ''Elementary Cryptanalysis''.
* [[Rosario Candela]], who used the nom ISKANDER, member since June 1934.
* [[David Kahn (writer)|David Kahn]], who used the noms DAKON, ISHCABIBEL and more recently Kahn D.
* [[Will Shortz]], ''[[The New York Times|New York Times]]'' Puzzle Editor, who uses the nom WILLz.
* [[David Shulman]], [[lexicographer]] and [[cryptographer]], member since 1933, who used the nom Ab Struse.
* [[James Gillogly]], who uses the nom SCRYER.
* [[Gelett Burgess]], American artist, art critic, poet, author and humorist, used the nom TWO O'CLOCK.
